column3:
Did you see something
move over there? I fought
it, but it fled.{page_break}When I came back it was
there again. Watching
the ash fall.{end_wait}
It's hiding again.\nSomething in this place\nis learning to hide.{end_wait}

It struck me from behind
and ran. Not a beast.
A beast would have stayed.{page_break}Next time I'll be
ready. I hope.{end_wait}
I know its kind.\nIt will be back, sooner\nor later. They always are.{end_wait}
What is it?{pause_20_skippable} Yeh want tae\ngo intae that cursed\nforest after all?{end_now}
Hmmm.{pause_20_skippable} Brave, or\nfools. In these times\nthere's little between.{end_wait}
Sorry, lads. Kolima is no\nplace for boys. Leave it\nto men who've buried kin.{end_wait}

I dreamt a bearded
warrior ended the curse.
In the dream he wept.{page_break}I wake up thinking it
cost him more than
it cost us.{end_wait}

They say travelers from
the Goma Range lifted
the curse.{page_break}Big men, they say.
Strong. But everyone says
that of anyone who wins.{page_break}Tret was only a spirit
in pain. I hope they
know what they did.{end_wait}

Bearded men freed Kolima
from the curse, they say.
Who were they, really?{page_break}If you meet them, tell
them Kolima remembers.{end_wait}
All warriors are big.\nAll warriors have beards.\nSo the children say.{end_wait}

Fuchin Temple lies across
the river. Pilgrims still
walk there, ash or not.{page_break}Visit it, if you have
time. Few of us do now.{end_wait}

Our blades are the best
you will find, and the
price just went up.{page_break}Altin sells weapons too,
south of the river. If
they still open doors.{end_wait}
Altin's steel is good.\nMine is better, and\nmine is here.{end_wait}
